contexts.text: Which were gifts given to Jehovah, and were called heave-offerings.
The flank of the heave-offering () = the Divine Celestial which is of the Lord alone perceived in Heaven and the Church... The heave-offering = what is given and received.
Which is shaken, and which is heaved up () = which is acknowledged and which is perceived... What is heaved up = the Divine Celestial which is of the Lord alone perceived in Heaven and in the Church.

As regards the heave-offering, that is called a heave-offering which was for Jehovah or the Lord, and was given to Aaron for the sake of the representation; and as Aaron represented the Lord as to Divine good, therefore that which was heaved up from the sacrifices, and was given to Aaron, represented the Divine of the Lord, and is also called the anointing. Illustrated, Explained... From these things it is evident what is meant by the heave-offerings; namely, that all things were so called which are Jehovah's, that is, the Lord's.

The heave-offerings are called gifts given to Jehovah... but it is meant that they are Jehovah's not from any gift, but from possession... and therefore it is said, Because this is the heave-offering, and the heave-offering shall be from with the sons of Israel, it is a heave-offering to Jehovah (), by which is signified that the heave-offering from the sons of Israel is Jehovah's heave-offering; thus that the gift from them is a gift from the Lord. Hence it is evident what the heave-offering is.
Because this is the heave-offering () = a representative of the Divine good and of the Divine truth thence proceeding.

And the heave-offering shall be from with the sons of Israel from their peace-sacrifices, it is a heave-offering to Jehovah () = reception in the Heavens and the Church, and in the acknowledgement that it is of the Lord alone.
The heave-offering from them = that it is of the Lord alone.
The half of a shekel a heave-offering to Jehovah () = that all things of truth from good are of the Lord alone... A heave-offering to Jehovah = the things which are of the Lord alone.
He shall give a heave-offering to Jehovah () = ascription to Jehovah. A heave-offering to Jehovah = that which is of the Lord alone...
By the lifting up of the hands () the like is signified as by the meat-offering.

Therefore, to Aaron and his sons were given holy things of the sons of Israel, which were gifts given to Jehovah, and were called heave-offerings; and it is said that they are the anointing, or for the anointing; that is, that they are a representation... of the Lord and of the Divine things which are from him. Illustrated.
